'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Pete Ricketts]]{{efn|In January 2023, Ricketts was appointed by Governor [[Jim Pillen]] to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Senator [[Ben Sasse]], who had become the president of [[University of Florida]].}} | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Pete Ricketts]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Nebraska}} The '''2024 United States Senate special election in Nebraska''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[Classes of United States senators|Class 2]] member of the [[United States Senate]] from [[Nebraska]], to complete the term of [[Ben Sasse]], who resigned on January 8, 2023, to become the president of the [[University of Florida]].{{Cite web |last=Hammel |first=Paul |date=December 5, 2022 |title=Ben Sasse makes it official, will resign U.S. Senate seat Jan. 8 |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/briefs/ben-sasse-makes-it-official-will-resign-u-s-senate-seat-jan-8/ |access-date=December 6, 2022 |website=Nebraska Examiner |language=en-US}} On January 12, 2023, Governor [[Jim Pillen]] appointed [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former Governor [[Pete Ricketts]] to fill the seat until the election. Ricketts won the special election, defeating Democratic nominee [[Preston Love Jr.]] with 62.5% of the vote. This was the first time since [[1954 United States Senate elections|1954]] where both of Nebraska's U.S. Senate seats were concurrently up for election. Primary elections took place on May 14, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Ricketts [[2024 Nebraska elections|outperformed other Republicans]] who faced contested statewide elections in this cycle. {{toclimit|3}} ==Appointment== Republican [[Pete Ricketts]], former [[List of governors of Nebraska|governor of Nebraska]] (2015–2023) and nominee for the U.S. Senate in [[2006 United States Senate election in Nebraska|2006]], was appointed on January 12, 2023 by Governor Jim Pillen.{{cite news |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/01/12/politics/pete-ricketts-senate/index.html |title=Nebraska Gov. Pillen appoints Pete Ricketts to Sasse's Senate seat |last=Bradner |first=Eric |work=[[CNN]] |date=January 12, 2023}} Ricketts' appointment was met with controversy as Ricketts had financially supported Pillen's 2022 gubernatorial campaign.{{cite web |last1=Sanderford |first1=Aaron |title=Pillen, as expected, taps former Gov. Pete Ricketts to succeed Sasse in Senate • Nebraska Examiner |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2023/01/12/pillen-as-expected-taps-former-gov-pete-ricketts-to-succeed-sasse-in-senate/ |website=Nebraska Examiner |access-date=7 April 2025 |date=12 January 2023}} === Applied to be appointed === In total, 111 individuals submitted applications for Sasse's seat, and nine candidates were interviewed by Pillen.{{Cite web |author1=Stoddard, Martha |author2=Bamer, Erin |title=Pillen appoints former Gov.
